    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot

      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the

2. `_ompVersion` regex: `omp v(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)` — but the welcome banner shows "omp v18.2.8" while provenance.json has `"omp_version": null`. Why null? `_ompVersion(harness.screenText)` — maybe screenText at the end of the test (after tool turn) no longer contains the welcome banner — it scrolls off. So omp_version recorded null despite the version being 18.2.8 in fixtures. That's a real bug in provenance: version should be captured from the boot screen, not from the final screen. The comment says "from the captured banner" but it's called after all the turns. Result: provenance.json has omp_version: null. IMPORTANT? It undermines provenance fidelity — future recaptures can't tell which omp version the fixtures came from (only commit sha). And PR description claims provenance correctness. I'd rate IMPORTANT (provenance fidelity) — actually is it blocking? The parity suite asserts omp_commit pins, not version. The null version is a data-quality gap. IMPORTANT feels right, or SUGGESTION. Per "when in doubt start one level higher" — IMPORTANT.

Also note the PR description says "bun 1.2.19" but provenance.json says "1.4.2" — documentation inconsistency in the PR body (provenance is authoritative). SUGGESTION.

3. Wait — bigger issue: **the captured txt shows "Update Available — New version 18.6.0"** — a network-fetched update banner baked into the fixture. If omp's release moves, a recapture with the same pinned commit would still show the same banner (pinned commit → same version 18.2.8, and update check fetches latest; banner content would drift over time). This makes recaptures non-deterministic: the update banner will change whenever oh-my-pi releases a new version, forcing fixture churn unrelated to the pin. Should disable update checks (or scrub). The update banner is volatile content committed into fixtures; a recapture a month later will differ even at the same commit. The scrub might handle... no, "Update Available"/"New version 18.6.0" — the version number "18.6.0" would scrub to <num> by generic number rule, but the row presence itself might vary (if no update available, rows disappear → chrome row count changes → parity diff). pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks — the cli_visual harness
      # spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` from the repo root and its boot budget
      # must not pay the cold-hook cost (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

## Delivered

Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.
- **Root REG suite green WITH fixtures, no skips** (\`dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart\`: 6/6): welcome screen, status bar structure, separator glyph inventory, sticky footer, code fence, provenance geometry.
- **Capture test hardening** (first real capture surfaced these): omp theme pinned to dark + asserted in omp's settings; \`statusLine.nerdSymbols\` written and round-trip-verified through omp's strict settings parser; \`statusLinePreset\` default enforced (compact single line); boot-check reorder.
- **Parity wiring fixes**: \`tui.statusLine.nerdSymbols\` knob on the fa side (strict bool, yaml round-trip, 94/94 existing status-line tests green); separator glyphs bridge powerline-thin when a preset carries no explicit separators; preset \`''\` resolves to the default preset; normalizer scrub extended to nerd glyphs (U+F000+), numeric cost/pct forms, gauge patterns.
- **Golden-guard PTY-orphan checks** exercised by the green capture run (config-leak + PTY cleanup in \`close()\`).
- **fa visual leg bug fix**: \`bootDiff\` interpolated a \`Directory\` object into the twin path (\`Directory: '...'\`) - crashed on its first-ever fixture-backed run; now uses \`.path\`.

## Remaining (real product-level parity drift, needs its own lane)
The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work, not wiring:
1. **Welcome/idle chrome**: fa 13 non-separator chrome rows vs omp 27 - omp's welcome box/tips art is structurally richer; fa's own welcome design differs.
2. **Tool-call chrome**: omp renders boxed tool cards (11 chrome-heavy rows) vs fa 1 - card border rendering not ported.

pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks — the cli_visual harness
      # spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` from the repo root and its boot budget
      # must not pay the cold-hook cost (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T19:45:37Z

## PR Description

Fixes #918 (fixture capture + wiring leg; #810 AC7.1 done, AC7.4 partially - see Remaining).

## Delivered
- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.
- **Root REG suite green WITH fixtures, no skips** (\`dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart\`: 6/6): welcome screen, status bar structure, separator glyph inventory, sticky footer, code fence, provenance geometry.
- **Capture test hardening** (first real capture surfaced these): omp theme pinned to dark + asserted in omp's settings; \`statusLine.nerdSymbols\` written and round-trip-verified through omp's strict settings parser; \`statusLinePreset\` default enforced (compact single line); boot-check reorder.
- **Parity wiring fixes**: \`tui.statusLine.nerdSymbols\` knob on the fa side (strict bool, yaml round-trip, 94/94 existing status-line tests green); separator glyphs bridge powerline-thin when a preset carries no explicit separators; preset \`''\` resolves to the default preset; normalizer scrub extended to nerd glyphs (U+F000+), numeric cost/pct forms, gauge patterns.
- **Golden-guard PTY-orphan checks** exercised by the green capture run (config-leak + PTY cleanup in \`close()\`).
- **fa visual leg bug fix**: \`bootDiff\` interpolated a \`Directory\` object into the twin path (\`Directory: '...'\`) - crashed on its first-ever fixture-backed run; now uses \`.path\`.

## Remaining (real product-level parity drift, needs its own lane)
The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work, not wiring:
1. **Welcome/idle chrome**: fa 13 non-separator chrome rows vs omp 27 - omp's welcome box/tips art is structurally richer; fa's own welcome design differs.
2. **Tool-call chrome**: omp renders boxed tool cards (11 chrome-heavy rows) vs fa 1 - card border rendering not ported.
3. **Status bar gauge architecture**: omp embeds the context gauge in the band gap behind the powerline cap (fused into the trailing segment); fa paints it as a separate trailing segment; brand-leading segment differs (fa text logo vs omp π icon). The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

## Evidence
- Capture: green, wrote twins + provenance (cost-segment policy enforced at capture time).
- Root parity: \`00:00 +6: All tests passed!\`
- fa visual leg: runs against fixtures; 3 structural findings listed above (exact signatures in the run log).
- \`tui_status_line_test\`: 94/94 green with the new knob.

      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)

          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"

          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version

        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.

pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks — the cli_visual harness
      # spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` from the repo root and its boot budget
      # must not pay the cold-hook cost (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

    name: Coverage ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [changes, test-core]
    timeout-minutes: 5

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

Fixes #918 (fixture capture + wiring leg; #810 AC7.1 done, AC7.4 partially - see Remaining).

## Delivered
- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.
- **Root REG suite green WITH fixtures, no skips** (\`dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart\`: 6/6): welcome screen, status bar structure, separator glyph inventory, sticky footer, code fence, provenance geometry.
- **Capture test hardening** (first real capture surfaced these): omp theme pinned to dark + asserted in omp's settings; \`statusLine.nerdSymbols\` written and round-trip-verified through omp's strict settings parser; \`statusLinePreset\` default enforced (compact single line); boot-check reorder.
- **Parity wiring fixes**: \`tui.statusLine.nerdSymbols\` knob on the fa side (strict bool, yaml round-trip, 94/94 existing status-line tests green); separator glyphs bridge powerline-thin when a preset carries no explicit separators; preset \`''\` resolves to the default preset; normalizer scrub extended to nerd glyphs (U+F000+), numeric cost/pct forms, gauge patterns.
- **Golden-guard PTY-orphan checks** exercised by the green capture run (config-leak + PTY cleanup in \`close()\`).
- **fa visual leg bug fix**: \`bootDiff\` interpolated a \`Directory\` object into the twin path (\`Directory: '...'\`) - crashed on its first-ever fixture-backed run; now uses \`.path\`.

## Remaining (real product-level parity drift, needs its own lane)
The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work, not wiring:
1. **Welcome/idle chrome**: fa 13 non-separator chrome rows vs omp 27 - omp's welcome box/tips art is structurally richer; fa's own welcome design differs.
2. **Tool-call chrome**: omp renders boxed tool cards (11 chrome-heavy rows) vs fa 1 - card border rendering not ported.
3. **Status bar gauge architecture**: omp embeds the context gauge in the band gap behind the powerline cap (fused into the trailing segment); fa paints it as a separate trailing segment; brand-leading segment differs (fa text logo vs omp π icon). The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

## Evidence
- Capture: green, wrote twins + provenance (cost-segment policy enforced at capture time).
- Root parity: \`00:00 +6: All tests passed!\`
- fa visual leg: runs against fixtures; 3 structural findings listed above (exact signatures in the run log).
- \`tui_status_line_test\`: 94/94 green with the new knob.

pty-visual:

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot

      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the

## PR Description

Fixes #918 (fixture capture + wiring leg; #810 AC7.1 done, AC7.4 partially - see Remaining).

## Delivered
- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.
- **Root REG suite green WITH fixtures, no skips** (\`dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart\`: 6/6): welcome screen, status bar structure, separator glyph inventory, sticky footer, code fence, provenance geometry.
- **Capture test hardening** (first real capture surfaced these): omp theme pinned to dark + asserted in omp's settings; \`statusLine.nerdSymbols\` written and round-trip-verified through omp's strict settings parser; \`statusLinePreset\` default enforced (compact single line); boot-check reorder.
- **Parity wiring fixes**: \`tui.statusLine.nerdSymbols\` knob on the fa side (strict bool, yaml round-trip, 94/94 existing status-line tests green); separator glyphs bridge powerline-thin when a preset carries no explicit separators; preset \`''\` resolves to the default preset; normalizer scrub extended to nerd glyphs (U+F000+), numeric cost/pct forms, gauge patterns.
- **Golden-guard PTY-orphan checks** exercised by the green capture run (config-leak + PTY cleanup in \`close()\`).
- **fa visual leg bug fix**: \`bootDiff\` interpolated a \`Directory\` object into the twin path (\`Directory: '...'\`) - crashed on its first-ever fixture-backed run; now uses \`.path\`.

## Remaining (real product-level parity drift, needs its own lane)
The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work, not wiring:
1. **Welcome/idle chrome**: fa 13 non-separator chrome rows vs omp 27 - omp's welcome box/tips art is structurally richer; fa's own welcome design differs.
2. **Tool-call chrome**: omp renders boxed tool cards (11 chrome-heavy rows) vs fa 1 - card border rendering not ported.
3. **Status bar gauge architecture**: omp embeds the context gauge in the band gap behind the powerline cap (fused into the trailing segment); fa paints it as a separate trailing segment; brand-leading segment differs (fa text logo vs omp π icon). The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

## Evidence
- Capture: green, wrote twins + provenance (cost-segment policy enforced at capture time).
- Root parity: \`00:00 +6: All tests passed!\`
- fa visual leg: runs against fixtures; 3 structural findings listed above (exact signatures in the run log).
- \`tui_status_line_test\`: 94/94 green with the new knob.

Also, since the bar is identical in both, the parity suite's "status bar structure" leg is really just re-testing the boot frame. It's documented in-test though. SUGGESTION at most.

2. `_ompVersion` regex: `omp v(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)` — but the welcome banner shows "omp v18.2.8" while provenance.json has `"omp_version": null`. Why null? `_ompVersion(harness.screenText)` — maybe screenText at the end of the test (after tool turn) no longer contains the welcome banner — it scrolls off. So omp_version recorded null despite the version being 18.2.8 in fixtures. That's a real bug in provenance: version should be captured from the boot screen, not from the final screen. The comment says "from the captured banner" but it's called after all the turns. Result: provenance.json has omp_version: null. IMPORTANT? It undermines provenance fidelity — future recaptures can't tell which omp version the fixtures came from (only commit sha). And PR description claims provenance correctness. I'd rate IMPORTANT (provenance fidelity) — actually is it blocking? The parity suite asserts omp_commit pins, not version. The null version is a data-quality gap. Also note the PR description says "bun 1.2.19" but provenance.json says "1.4.2" — documentation inconsistency in the PR body (provenance is authoritative). SUGGESTION.

3. Wait — bigger issue: **the captured txt shows "Update Available — New version 18.6.0"** — a network-fetched update banner baked into the fixture. If omp's release moves, a recapture with the same pinned commit would still show the same banner (pinned commit → same version 18.2.8, and update check fetches latest; banner content would drift over time). This makes recaptures non-deterministic: the update banner will change whenever oh-my-pi releases a new version, forcing fixture churn unrelated to the pin. Should disable update checks (or scrub). SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? It affects fixture stability — IMPORTANT-ish. It's drift-prone; I'd say SUGGESTION to IMPORTANT. I'll flag as IMPORTANT? Hmm. The update banner is volatile content committed into fixtures; a recapture a month later will differ even at the same commit. The scrub might handle... no, "Update Available"/"New version 18.6.0" — the version number "18.6.0" would scrub to <num> by generic number rule, but the row presence itself might vary (if no update available, rows disappear → chrome row count changes → parity diff). That's real nondeterminism. I'd rate IMPORTANT.

4. The fixture bar shows gauge "8%" while fa renders 46000/2000 = 23% — scrub handles pct. Fine.

5. The capture test writes config.yml with `symbolPreset: nerd` and theme; test asserts round-trip through omp's strict settings parser — per PR description, asserted. Where's the assertion? The PR says "statusLine.nerdSymbols written and round-trip-verified through omp's strict settings parser; statusLinePreset default enforced (compact single line); boot-check reorder". But the current capture test only writes config.yml with symbolPreset + theme dark; I don't see a statusLine.nerdSymbols write or statusLinePreset enforcement in the diff. Maybe that's on the fa side... The PR description mentions things not visible in the diff (boot-check reorder). The diff shown is truncated in the middle (20131 chars omitted) — the flutter_app diffs I saw are complete from git. The "boot-check reorder" isn't in the diff... Maybe PR description overstated. Not a finding per se.

6. `kRegSeparatorGlyphs` change: 'powerline-thin' from E0B2 to E0B1. Need to check fa's StatusLineSeparatorStyle.powerlineThin actually renders E0B1 — the comment claims verified. Let me check tui_status_line.dart for the glyph table.

7. In `parseStatusLineConfig` — `_statusLineBoolFlag` returns `value as bool?` after null/bool check. Fine.

8. `resolveStatusLineSpec`: `nerdSymbols: config?.nerdSymbols ?? preset.nerd`. Fine.

9. tui_status_line.dart `toYaml` — order of fields; round-trip test covers.

10. In the fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart diff: added `nerdSymbols: true` yaml in fa config. Fine.

11. The parity test change: `faSig.length >= ompSig.length` — a weakened assertion. With documented reason. But `expect(faSig.length, greaterThanOrEqualTo(ompSig.length))` — if omp's bar gains segments, this could pass while real drift occurs? It only checks fa has at least as many segments. Weak but documented. Also `contains('<word:2>')` etc. This is a deliberate weakening; documented in-test. Reviewer might flag that `greaterThanOrEqualTo` + contains checks could pass with a substantially different bar (e.g., fa renders extra junk segments). But that's the documented trade-off. SUGGESTION maybe not needed.

Also note the fa bar render: spec = resolveStatusLineSpec(const StatusLineConfig(nerdSymbols: true)) — with preset null → default preset. Fine.

12. Security: `--api-key dummy-reg-capture`, fine. HOME override hermetic. PATH env constructed via substring on bunBin path — if bunBin has no '/', lastIndexOf returns -1 → substring(0,-1) throws. _findBun candidates all contain '/', so OK.

15. The fixture `04_code_block.txt` bar shows `─────8%────...󰕝────󰁨────────200K─` — contains 󰁨 glyph (cost?) but cost policy asserts bar in 02 has no '$'. OK.

pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)

    permissions:

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1231
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1231
- **Title**: fix(918): omp_ref reference fixtures captured on PTY host + nerd-glyph parity wiring
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/918-omp-ref-fixtures` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +309
- **Deletions**: -32
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T15:25:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T19:45:37Z

## PR Description

Fixes #918 (fixture capture + wiring leg; #810 AC7.1 done, AC7.4 partially - see Remaining).

## Delivered
- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.
- **Root REG suite green WITH fixtures, no skips** (\`dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart\`: 6/6): welcome screen, status bar structure, separator glyph inventory, sticky footer, code fence, provenance geometry.
- **Capture test hardening** (first real capture surfaced these): omp theme pinned to dark + asserted in omp's settings; \`statusLine.nerdSymbols\` written and round-trip-verified through omp's strict settings parser; \`statusLinePreset\` default enforced (compact single line); boot-check reorder.
- **Parity wiring fixes**: \`tui.statusLine.nerdSymbols\` knob on the fa side (strict bool, yaml round-trip, 94/94 existing status-line tests green); separator glyphs bridge powerline-thin when a preset carries no explicit separators; preset \`''\` resolves to the default preset; normalizer scrub extended to nerd glyphs (U+F000+), numeric cost/pct forms, gauge patterns.
- **Golden-guard PTY-orphan checks** exercised by the green capture run (config-leak + PTY cleanup in \`close()\`).
- **fa visual leg bug fix**: \`bootDiff\` interpolated a \`Directory\` object into the twin path (\`Directory: '...'\`) - crashed on its first-ever fixture-backed run; now uses \`.path\`.

## Remaining (real product-level parity drift, needs its own lane)
The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work, not wiring:
1. **Welcome/idle chrome**: fa 13 non-separator chrome rows vs omp 27 - omp's welcome box/tips art is structurally richer; fa's own welcome design differs.
2. **Tool-call chrome**: omp renders boxed tool cards (11 chrome-heavy rows) vs fa 1 - card border rendering not ported.
3. **Status bar gauge architecture**: omp embeds the context gauge in the band gap behind the powerline cap (fused into the trailing segment); fa paints it as a separate trailing segment; brand-leading segment differs (fa text logo vs omp π icon). The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

## Evidence
- Capture: green, wrote twins + provenance (cost-segment policy enforced at capture time).
- Root parity: \`00:00 +6: All tests passed!\`
- fa visual leg: runs against fixtures; 3 structural findings listed above (exact signatures in the run log).
- \`tui_status_line_test\`: 94/94 green with the new knob.

blocks.text:
Key observations on the capture test:

1. Screenshots 01 and 02 are taken of the SAME boot frame, one after another. The comment says "the twin exists so the bar diff has a dedicated fixture." But both `.txt` twins are byte-identical (blob c4116a9) and PNGs are the same size (118353 bytes — likely identical images too). So `02_status_bar_default` is a literal duplicate of `01_welcome_idle`. Is that a problem? The parity test uses 02 for bar structure; but it means the "status bar default" fixture adds no new information — it's the welcome screen. It's redundant but intentional per the comment. However, the cost-segment policy check reads bar from 02 — fine. Hmm — is it worth flagging? Suggestion-level: duplicate fixtures double maintenance; a future welcome-screen change will require both twins to be updated identically. Also, since the bar is identical in both, the parity suite's "status bar structure" leg is really just re-testing the boot frame. It's documented in-test though. SUGGESTION at most.

2. `_ompVersion` regex: `omp v(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)` — but the welcome banner shows "omp v18.2.8" while provenance.json has `"omp_version": null`. Why null? `_ompVersion(harness.screenText)` — maybe screenText at the end of the test (after tool turn) no longer contains the welcome banner — it scrolls off.     name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks — the cli_visual harness
      # spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` from the repo root and its boot budget
      # must not pay the cold-hook cost (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

  coverage-gate:
    name: Coverage ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [changes, test-core]
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks — the cli_visual harness
      # spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` from the repo root and its boot budget
      # must not pay the cold-hook cost (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.

The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work, not wiring:

pty-visual:

    steps:
