      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:

Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

Key observations on the capture test:

1. Screenshots 01 and 02 are taken of the SAME boot frame, one after another. The comment says "the twin exists so the bar diff has a dedicated fixture." But both `.txt` twins are byte-identical (blob c4116a9) and PNGs are the same size (118353 bytes — likely identical images too). So `02_status_bar_default` is a literal duplicate of `01_welcome_idle`. Is that a problem? The parity test uses 02 for bar structure; but it means the "status bar default" fixture adds no new information — it's the welcome screen. It's redundant but intentional per the comment. However, the cost-segment policy check reads bar from 02 — fine. Hmm — is it worth flagging? Suggestion-level: duplicate fixtures double maintenance; a future welcome-screen change will require both twins to be updated identically. Also, since the bar is identical in both, the parity suite's "status bar structure" leg is really just re-testing the boot frame. It's documented in-test though. SUGGESTION at most.

2. `_ompVersion` regex: `omp v(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)` — but the welcome banner shows "omp v18.2.8" while provenance.json has `"omp_version": null`. Why null? `_ompVersion(harness.screenText)` — maybe screenText at the end of the test (after tool turn) no longer contains the welcome banner — it scrolls off. So omp_version recorded null despite the version being 18.2.8 in fixtures. That's a real bug in provenance: version should be captured from the boot screen, not from the final screen. The comment says "from the captured banner" but it's called after all the turns. Result: provenance.json has omp_version: null. IMPORTANT? It undermines provenance fidelity — future recaptures can't tell which omp version the fixtures came from (only commit sha). And PR description claims provenance correctness. I'd rate IMPORTANT (provenance fidelity) — actually is it blocking? The parity suite asserts omp_commit pins, not version. The null version is a data-quality gap. IMPORTANT feels right, or SUGGESTION. Per "when in doubt start one level higher" — IMPORTANT.

Also note the PR description says "bun 1.2.19" but provenance.json says "1.4.2" — documentation inconsistency in the PR body (provenance is authoritative). SUGGESTION.

3. Wait — bigger issue: **the captured txt shows "Update Available — New version 18.6.0"** — a network-fetched update banner baked into the fixture. If omp's release moves, a recapture with the same pinned commit would still show the same banner (pinned commit → same version 18.2.8, and update check fetches latest; banner content would drift over time). This makes recaptures non-deterministic: the update banner will change whenever oh-my-pi releases a new version, forcing fixture churn unrelated to the pin. Should disable update checks (or scrub). SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? It affects fixture stability — IMPORTANT-ish. It's drift-prone; I'd say SUGGESTION to IMPORTANT. I'll flag as IMPORTANT? Hmm. The update banner is volatile content committed into fixtures; a recapture a month later will differ even at the same commit. The scrub might handle... no, "Update Available"/"New version 18.6.0" — the version number "18.6.0" would scrub to <num> by generic number rule, but the row presence itself might vary (if no update available, rows disappear → chrome row count changes → parity diff). That's real nondeterminism. I'd rate IMPORTANT.

4. The fixture bar shows gauge "8%" while fa renders 46000/2000 = 23% — scrub handles pct. Fine.

5. The capture test writes config.yml with `symbolPreset: nerd` and theme; test asserts round-trip through omp's strict settings parser — per PR description, asserted. Where's the assertion? The PR says "statusLine.nerdSymbols written and round-trip-verified through omp's strict settings parser; statusLinePreset default enforced (compact single line); boot-check reorder". Maybe that's on the fa side... The PR description mentions things not visible in the diff (boot-check reorder). The diff shown is truncated in the middle (20131 chars omitted) — the flutter_app diffs I saw are complete from git. The "boot-check reorder" isn't in the diff... Maybe PR description overstated. Not a finding per se.

9. tui_status_line.dart `toYaml` — order of fields; round-trip test covers.

10. In the fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart diff: added `nerdSymbols: true` yaml in fa config. Fine.

But `expect(faSig.length, greaterThanOrEqualTo(ompSig.length))` — if omp's bar gains segments, this could pass while real drift occurs? It only checks fa has at least as many segments. Weak but documented. Also `contains('<word:2>')` etc. This is a deliberate weakening; documented in-test. pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks — the cli_visual harness
      # spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` from the repo root and its boot budget
      # must not pay the cold-hook cost (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the fa-side PTY parity leg fails 3/3 against these fixtures — `pty-visual` is a required quality-gate leg**

I ran the leg locally on this head (`cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual/fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart --tags integration`): **0 passed, 3 failed**, with exactly the structural differences the PR description lists under "Remaining":

- `welcome/idle + status bar`: `01_welcome_idle: segment count differs — fa 5 [<word:1>, <path>, <word:1>, <path>, <pct>], omp 3 [<word:0>, <word:2>, <word:4>]` (plus chrome-row drift)
- `streaming turn with one tool call`: chrome rows fa 1 vs omp 11
- `fenced code block`: chrome rows fa 2 vs omp 21

`pty-visual` runs `flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration` and is in the `quality-gate` `needs:` list (ci.yml), so as shipped this PR turns a merge-blocking leg permanently red. Declaring the drift out-of-scope for #918 is fine; leaving strict assertions that always fail is not — CI can't distinguish "known porting drift" from a new regression.

Fix within this PR's scope (before the porting lane lands), e.g.:

- Add an **expected-findings allow-list** to the flutter leg: run `structuralDiff`/`_diffTurnChrome`, assert the returned findings are *exactly* the documented set (fail on any NEW finding), or
- Replace the known-drift sub-assertions (`bootDiff(...) isEmpty`, chrome-row equality on turn screens) with named, ticket-referencing `skip`s until the porting lane closes them.

Either keeps `pty-visual` green and sensitive to new drift. The root plain-Dart suite stays as the strict merge-blocking surface (verified 6/6 green locally).

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the committed `provenance.json` has `"omp_version": null` — the version is read after the banner scrolls away**

`'omp_version': _ompVersion(harness.screenText)` runs at the END of the capture, after the code-block and tool-call turns — by then the welcome banner (`omp v18.2.8`, visible in all four committed twins) has scrolled off screen, the regex finds nothing and provenance records `null`. The committed `provenance.json` confirms it.

The version is exactly the kind of data provenance exists for (the commit sha alone doesn't tell you which release series the fixtures depict). Capture it while the boot frame is on screen — right around the `01_welcome_idle`/`02_status_bar_default` screenshots — and consider asserting `omp_version != null` in the root suite's provenance test so a future regression here is caught.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a live network-fetched "Update Available" banner is baked into every reference fixture**

Rows 23–25 of this twin (`Update Available` / `New version 18.6.0 is available. Run: omp update`) come from omp's online update check, not from the pinned commit. Consequences:

- Any future re-capture at the SAME pinned commit will produce different twins the moment oh-my-pi publishes a new release (banner text changes), or lose these rows entirely if no update is available (chrome row count changes → parity diff fires for reasons unrelated to the pin).
- The fixtures — whose whole point is determinism — silently depend on the network state of the capturing host.

The capture already builds a hermetic agent dir (`config.yml`); add whatever update-check disable omp supports there (or block the update endpoint for the child), or extend the normalizer to scrub/collapse the update-banner rows. Without one of these, the "re-capture when the pin moves" workflow from the capture-test header will churn fixtures on every upstream release.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `02_status_bar_default` is byte-identical to `01_welcome_idle` (both PNG and TXT)**

`md5sum` on the committed twins: the two `.txt` files hash identically, and both `.png` files hash identically (`06eb3804…`). The "dedicated bar fixture" therefore adds no independent signal — every check against `02` would pass/fail exactly as against `01`. It also doubles fixture churn: any welcome-screen change in a future re-capture must produce two identical files, and nothing currently fails if a capture glitch makes them silently diverge.

Either drop `02` and point the bar checks at `01`, or keep the two-stem convention but add a capture-time assertion that the twins are identical (pinning the "same boot frame" intent in code).

- **PR #**: 1231

- **Title**: fix(918): omp_ref reference fixtures captured on PTY host + nerd-glyph parity wiring
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/918-omp-ref-fixtures` → `main`

- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T19:45:37Z

## PR Description

Fixes #918 (fixture capture + wiring leg; #810 AC7.1 done, AC7.4 partially - see Remaining).

## Delivered
- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.
- **Root REG suite green WITH fixtures, no skips** (\`dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart\`: 6/6): welcome screen, status bar structure, separator glyph inventory, sticky footer, code fence, provenance geometry.
- **Capture test hardening** (first real capture surfaced these): omp theme pinned to dark + asserted in omp's settings; \`statusLine.nerdSymbols\` written and round-trip-verified through omp's strict settings parser; \`statusLinePreset\` default enforced (compact single line); boot-check reorder.
- **Parity wiring fixes**: \`tui.statusLine.nerdSymbols\` knob on the fa side (strict bool, yaml round-trip, 94/94 existing status-line tests green); separator glyphs bridge powerline-thin when a preset carries no explicit separators; preset \`''\` resolves to the default preset; normalizer scrub extended to nerd glyphs (U+F000+), numeric cost/pct forms, gauge patterns.
- **Golden-guard PTY-orphan checks** exercised by the green capture run (config-leak + PTY cleanup in \`close()\`).
- **fa visual leg bug fix**: \`bootDiff\` interpolated a \`Directory\` object into the twin path (\`Directory: '...'\`) - crashed on its first-ever fixture-backed run; now uses \`.path\`.

## Remaining (real product-level parity drift, needs its own lane)
The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work, not wiring:
1. **Welcome/idle chrome**: fa 13 non-separator chrome rows vs omp 27 - omp's welcome box/tips art is structurally richer; fa's own welcome design differs.
2. **Tool-call chrome**: omp renders boxed tool cards (11 chrome-heavy rows) vs fa 1 - card border rendering not ported.
3. **Status bar gauge architecture**: omp embeds the context gauge in the band gap behind the powerline cap (fused into the trailing segment); fa paints it as a separate trailing segment; brand-leading segment differs (fa text logo vs omp π icon). The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

## Evidence
- Capture: green, wrote twins + provenance (cost-segment policy enforced at capture time).
- Root parity: \`00:00 +6: All tests passed!\`
- fa visual leg: runs against fixtures; 3 structural findings listed above (exact signatures in the run log).
- \`tui_status_line_test\`: 94/94 green with the new knob.

      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash

          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the

pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks — the cli_visual harness
      # spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` from the repo root and its boot budget
      # must not pay the cold-hook cost (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

## PR Description

Fixes #918 (fixture capture + wiring leg; #810 AC7.1 done, AC7.4 partially - see Remaining).

## Delivered
- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.
- **Root REG suite green WITH fixtures, no skips** (\`dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart\`: 6/6): welcome screen, status bar structure, separator glyph inventory, sticky footer, code fence, provenance geometry.
- **Capture test hardening** (first real capture surfaced these): omp theme pinned to dark + asserted in omp's settings; \`statusLine.nerdSymbols\` written and round-trip-verified through omp's strict settings parser; \`statusLinePreset\` default enforced (compact single line); boot-check reorder.
- **Parity wiring fixes**: \`tui.statusLine.nerdSymbols\` knob on the fa side (strict bool, yaml round-trip, 94/94 existing status-line tests green); separator glyphs bridge powerline-thin when a preset carries no explicit separators; preset \`''\` resolves to the default preset; normalizer scrub extended to nerd glyphs (U+F000+), numeric cost/pct forms, gauge patterns.
- **Golden-guard PTY-orphan checks** exercised by the green capture run (config-leak + PTY cleanup in \`close()\`).
- **fa visual leg bug fix**: \`bootDiff\` interpolated a \`Directory\` object into the twin path (\`Directory: '...'\`) - crashed on its first-ever fixture-backed run; now uses \`.path\`.

## Remaining (real product-level parity drift, needs its own lane)
The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work, not wiring:
1. **Welcome/idle chrome**: fa 13 non-separator chrome rows vs omp 27 - omp's welcome box/tips art is structurally richer; fa's own welcome design differs.
2. **Tool-call chrome**: omp renders boxed tool cards (11 chrome-heavy rows) vs fa 1 - card border rendering not ported.
3. **Status bar gauge architecture**: omp embeds the context gauge in the band gap behind the powerline cap (fused into the trailing segment); fa paints it as a separate trailing segment; brand-leading segment differs (fa text logo vs omp π icon). The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

## Evidence
- Capture: green, wrote twins + provenance (cost-segment policy enforced at capture time).
- Root parity: \`00:00 +6: All tests passed!\`
- fa visual leg: runs against fixtures; 3 structural findings listed above (exact signatures in the run log).
- \`tui_status_line_test\`: 94/94 green with the new knob.

pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks — the cli_visual harness
      # spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` from the repo root and its boot budget
      # must not pay the cold-hook cost (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

- **Reference fixtures committed**: \`test/integration/screenshots/omp_ref/\` - 4 png+txt twins (welcome/idle, status bar default, tool call, code block) + provenance.json. Captured on a PTY-capable host per the issue command block: oh-my-pi @ \`df624f56b\`, bun 1.2.19, local MockLlmServer (\`mockcap/test-model\`), 131x36, theme.dark pinned.

The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work, not wiring:
1. **Welcome/idle chrome**: fa 13 non-separator chrome rows vs omp 27 - omp's welcome box/tips art is structurally richer; fa's own welcome design differs.
2. **Tool-call chrome**: omp renders boxed tool cards (11 chrome-heavy rows) vs fa 1 - card border rendering not ported.
3. **Status bar gauge architecture**: omp embeds the context gauge in the band gap behind the powerline cap (fused into the trailing segment); fa paints it as a separate trailing segment; brand-leading segment differs (fa text logo vs omp π icon). The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core (model segment, path segment, segment presence) instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test.
Closing these = porting omp's chrome rendering into fa's TUI (product scope, exceeds #918's fixture/wiring contract).

- Capture: green, wrote twins + provenance (cost-segment policy enforced at capture time).

Confirmed: 01 and 02 are byte-identical twins (both PNG and TXT). Intentional per capture test comment, but it means:
- The "status bar (default preset, boot)" fixture is literally a copy of the welcome fixture — the dedicated bar fixture adds no independent coverage, doubles fixture churn, and could mask a regression where the bar disappears if... actually no, the bar is part of the frame. It's redundant but documented in-test. SUGGESTION.

More significant findings:

**F1 (IMPORTANT): provenance.json `omp_version: null`** — `_ompVersion(harness.screenText)` is called at the END of the capture, after the tool turn; the welcome banner ("omp v18.2.8") has scrolled off, so the regex finds nothing and writes null. The committed provenance.json confirms: `"omp_version": null` while the twins clearly show "omp v18.2.8". The version should be captured from the boot screen (screenshot 01's text) before turns scroll it away. Fix: capture `_ompVersion` right after the welcome screenshot.

**F2 (IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION): "Update Available — New version 18.6.0" banner baked into fixtures.** This is a live network-fetched update notice. On any future re-capture (same pinned commit), the banner rows will differ as soon as oh-my-pi ships a new release — and if no update is available the rows disappear entirely, changing chrome row count and breaking the parity diff for reasons unrelated to the pin. Should be disabled in the hermetic agent config (e.g. an update-check opt-out) or scrubbed. Is there an omp setting? Unknown — suggest investigating update check disable. I'll flag IMPORTANT since it undermines fixture stability, the core purpose of this PR.

Hmm, actually severity: it's a latent flake source for future recaptures, not a bug in current tests. SUGGESTION-to-IMPORTANT. I'll go IMPORTANT per "when in doubt, start one level higher"? The rule says start one level higher when in doubt. Fixture instability is a real maintainability concern for the artifact this PR introduces. IMPORTANT.

**F3 (IMPORTANT): PR description claims deliverables absent from the diff**: (a) "normalizer scrub extended to nerd glyphs (U+F000+), numeric cost/pct forms, gauge patterns" — no such patterns in kVolatilePatterns (checked both main and PR; diff is +4/-1 lines only); (b) "preset '' resolves to the default preset" — `_statusLinePreset('')` throws on both sides; (c) "separator glyphs bridge powerline-thin when a preset carries no explicit separators" — no bridging code in the diff. Also description says "bun 1.2.19" but committed provenance says 1.4.2. Either the description is stale (describing an earlier iteration) or the changes are missing. For a machine-reviewed loop where description drives AC verification, this gap matters. IMPORTANT.

Wait — let me double check (a): maybe scrub extension exists in the parity test? No. kVolatilePatterns on the PR head — I read it; no nerd glyph patterns, no gauge patterns beyond \d+%. Numeric cost/pct: `\[\$\d+\.\d{2}\]` and `\d+%` exist — but were those on main already? The normalizer diff is only the glyph map comment change, so all scrub patterns predate this PR. Description overstates. Confirmed.

**F4 (SUGGESTION): identical 01/02 twins** — documented redundancy; suggest deriving 02 from 01 or asserting they're identical so drift can't make them silently differ. Actually there's a subtle hazard: if a future recapture captures the two screenshots at slightly different frames (e.g. bar updates between them), the twins diverge silently. A cheap guard: in the capture test, assert 01/02 txt twins are identical (or drop one). SUGGESTION.

**F5 (SUGGESTION): fixture bakes machine-specific temp path** `…_qsj0cgr0000gn/T/omp_capture_cwd_bUWIyx` in the status bar. The normalizer scrubs paths during comparison (pattern anchored on path chars — the abbreviated path "…_qsj0cgr0000gn/T/omp_capture_cwd_bUWIyx" contains no leading / so the path regex `(?:~|\.)?/[A-Za-z0-9._@/-]{2,}` won't match "…_qsj..." — wait, there's a "/" in "T/omp_capture_cwd" — the regex needs to start with ~, ., or /. In the bar the token is ` …_qsj0cgr0000gn/T/omp_capture_cwd_bUWIyx`. Does it start with "/"? No, starts with "…". Hmm, but segmentSignature: `token.contains('/')` → '<path>'. And findStatusBarRow/splitBarSegments — the fa side renders cwd '/reg-sandbox-cwd' → scrub → <path>. The omp side "…_qsj0cgr0000gn/T/omp_capture_cwd_bUWIyx" contains '/' → <path>. OK so comparison works. But the bar-signature test 'status bar: fa default preset shape equals' uses barSignature which relies on token.contains('/') → path. Fine. So machine-specific path is scrubbed by shape. Not an issue. Drop F5.

But wait — one more check on the scrub: the cwd token in the fixture is "…_qsj0cgr0000gn/T/omp_capture_cwd_bUWIyx" — it contains digits "0000gn" — generic number rule `\b\d+\b` — "0000gn"... \b between 0 and g? No, \d and \w... '0' followed by 'g' is both word chars, so \b\d+\b wouldn't match inside "0000gn". Fine.

**F6: chrome-row-count parity on boot screen** — fa 13 rows vs omp 27 is "Remaining" per the PR — but then `bootDiff('01_welcome_idle')` expects `isEmpty`, which includes `_chromeRowCountFinding`. If fa has 13 chrome rows vs omp 27, the diff is non-empty → the fa visual test would FAIL. The PR says the fa visual leg "reports genuine differences" — meaning the flutter test currently fails?? "The fa visual leg now RUNS against the fixtures (no skip-green) and reports genuine fa↔omp surface differences that are porting work". If bootDiff expects isEmpty and rows differ, the test fails. Unless the pty-visual job isn't merge-blocking or the row-count finding is somehow not triggered. Wait — the chrome row count finding compares non-empty trimmed rows. fa welcome 13 vs omp 27 → finding non-empty → test fails. Is the fa visual leg currently failing? The PR says "fa visual leg: runs against fixtures; 3 structural findings listed above". That phrasing suggests the leg surfaces them — maybe as failures. If the flutter test fails, CI (pty-visual job) is red. ci_failures.md is absent — no CI failures provided, implying CI is green or unknown. Hmm.

Let me check: is fa_omp_reg_visual_test part of merge-blocking CI? The root suite comment says the merge-blocking surface is the plain-dart suite + pty-visual job runs the flutter leg. If the flutter leg currently fails on chrome row counts, this PR would be red. Maybe the fa welcome screen actually renders 27 rows? The PR says fa 13 non-separator chrome rows vs omp 27 — but structuralDiff counts ALL non-empty rows, not non-separator. So they differ → bootDiff non-empty → expect isEmpty fails.

Unless... the pty-visual job only runs on PTY-capable hosts and is optional/skipped in CI. The root suite comment: "The flutter-side PTY parity (full screens + band pixels) lives in flutter_app/test/cli_visual/fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart, run by the pty-visual job." Is pty-visual merge-blocking? Let me check the workflow. Also, maybe the fa visual leg diffs only pass because structuralDiff on boot screen... no, row counts differ.

Actually wait — re-read the "Remaining" section: "The parity bar-shape test therefore asserts the shared structural core ... instead of whole-bar equality - the deviation is documented in-test." That's about the ROOT suite bar test (which they adjusted). For the flutter leg: "fa visual leg: runs against fixtures; 3 structural findings listed above (exact signatures in the run log)". "run log" — suggesting they ran it and it reports findings, i.e., FAILS. If the flutter leg fails, and it's merge-blocking, this PR can't merge — that would be BLOCKING. Let me check CI config for the pty-visual job and whether fa_omp_reg_visual_test currently passes.

pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Git bootstrap
      # (same as the flutter-tests leg): flutter_tools pulls the official
      # arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks — the cli_visual harness
      # spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` from the repo root and its boot budget
      # must not pay the cold-hook cost (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

# Rework: fix CI red on `fix/918-omp-ref-fixtures` (PR #1231)

## Issues/Notes

- **Failed checks**: `CRAP + duplication` (the `guards` CI job) and the aggregate `Quality gate` (which fails whenever any `guards` leg is red).
- **Root cause**: the `nerdSymbols` knob added in this PR pushed `parseStatusLineConfig` (`lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart`) from **CC 9 → CC 11** by inlining a second strict-bool validation block. Neither bool-throw branch (`transparent`, `nerdSymbols`) had a test, so the function sat at ~81% line coverage — CRAP ≈ `11²·(1−0.81)² + 11 ≈ 14.9`, over the `12.0` threshold pinned in `crap4dart.yaml`. The pre-PR CC 9 passed only by a hair (≈11.9); the PR tipped it over.
- All other `guards` legs were verified green locally with the CI-identical pipeline: `crap4dart check --baseline` (2 passed / 1 warning-severity), jscpd `0.816% < 1.0%`, `ci_fast_gate.sh --stages dupx` OK, `check_crap_guards.py` OK.

## Approach

  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
